attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is applied to each URL_RE match, and that match has no length bound. A long run of punctuation inside one URL-like token costs roughly quadratic time, and owner-written descriptions have no length cap, so every viewer pays this cost on page open.
attacks.evidence: const raw = m[0].replace(TRAILING_PUNCT, ''); ABSENT: any maximum length on item.description or on a URL token

attacks.claim: The PR promises truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens, but the out.length===0 fallback hard-slices a whitespace-free text token mid-word. The test named 'never splits a link or a word' asserts that exact mid-word cut, so the documented contract and the code disagree.
attacks.evidence: PR text: 'truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens'; else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') }); expect(truncate(tokenize('x'.repeat(400)), 280).tokens).toEqual([{ kind: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(280) }])

attacks.claim: A leading link longer than the limit is pushed whole and truncated is still returned as true. When the link is the whole description, the toggle reveals nothing new, and when text follows it, the 280-character collapse is bypassed for the long-URL case this PR targets.
attacks.evidence: else if (out.length === 0) { out.push(t); // a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing } return { tokens: out, truncated: true };

attacks.claim: The body uses white-space: pre-line, which wraps only at spaces, and the anchor renders the URL unbroken. A long URL can overflow a phone-width viewport, which is the stated primary use case. The diff adds no overflow-wrap or word-break rule, although global CSS may already handle this and the stylesheet is not shown.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no CSS change in the diff for .item-description__body or its anchors; existing style is white-space: pre-line

attacks.claim: Stripping a trailing ')' from every URL breaks balanced-parenthesis URLs such as Wikipedia-style paths, so the href points to a different page than the author wrote. The test pins this behavior, which suggests it is a deliberate trade-off for parenthesized links.
attacks.evidence: TRAILING_PUNCT strips ')' ; test: expect 'http://a.example/x).' to yield href 'http://a.example/x'

attacks.claim: Length accounting mixes UTF-16 units (value.length) with code points (Array.from), so the fallback can exceed the stated limit for emoji and other non-BMP text.
attacks.evidence: if (used + t.value.length <= limit) vs Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('')

attacks.claim: Whitespace-only or otherwise droppable overflow still sets truncated to true, which shows a Show more toggle that reveals identical content.
attacks.evidence: return { tokens: out, truncated: true }; (no check that dropped content is non-whitespace)

attacks.claim: When the only usable whitespace in the head is at index 0, cut is 0 and the cut > 0 test falls through to a mid-word hard cut instead of a word boundary.
attacks.evidence: const cut = head.search(/\s\S*$/); if (cut > 0) ... else if (out.length === 0) ...

attacks.claim: When the cut falls between tokens, the preceding text keeps its trailing space, so the ellipsis renders after a stray space.
attacks.evidence: truncate pushes text 'see ' before the link; ItemDescription appends {short.truncated && !expanded && '…'}

attacks.claim: The toggle changes its visible label and aria-expanded together, so screen readers announce the state twice. The usual pattern keeps the label constant and lets aria-expanded carry the state.

Visible link text is the raw owner string while href is the normalized url.href, so the displayed text can differ from the real destination, including IDN or lookalike hosts. rel attributes do not address this display gap.
attacks.evidence: return { kind: 'link', value: raw, href: url.href }; {t.value}

attacks.claim: Expanded state lives in component state with no key tied to the item, and token keys are array indexes. If the component instance is reused across items, expansion can carry over to a different description.
attacks.evidence: const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false); ... key={i}; ABSENT: key tied to item.id

attacks.claim: Expanded mode renders one DOM node per text run and link with no cap on description size, so very large owner descriptions grow the DOM without bound.
attacks.evidence: {(expanded ? all : short.tokens).map(...)} ABSENT: any maximum description length

attacks.claim: Tests do not cover the 280 versus 281 boundary, Show less, empty descriptions, ItemPage integration, or tokenize() directly. The test named 'collapse at a word boundary' never asserts a word boundary.
attacks.evidence: test('long descriptions collapse at a word boundary and expand') asserts only button state and link presence

attacks.claim: The 280-character threshold is not defined as characters, UTF-16 code units, or rendered width, so the requirement is underspecified.
attacks.evidence: 'Descriptions over 280 characters now render collapsed' with no unit definition in the artifact
